attempts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Fix the display orientation in reference3, a 1536x1024 Deep Orbit spectrogram lesson illustration. Image1 is canonical Farah identity authority. Image2 is Lab architecture only. Image3 is exact scene to repair, not identity authority. Keep Farah's canonical face, mature proportions, relaxed interested expression, gray lab coat, AR lens, seated working pose and muted sage/brass/charcoal palette.
Replace the strongly reclined trapezoid drafting display with a large UPRIGHT monitor on a physically plausible swivel pedestal at the LEFT. Its glass and bezel are a FRONTAL rectangle: horizontal level top and bottom, vertical parallel sides, no in-plane tilt or steep oblique foreshortening. Farah and camera are on the readable front side, Farah to the right and slightly nearer camera. The monitor should comfortably use the left half of frame and face her. Keep a three-quarter view of her recognizable face, looking toward the diagram and speaking with engaged curiosity, not looking at camera. Her left hand rests simply on the desk, with clear five-finger anatomy; her right hand holds one straight stylus in a natural grip, pointing to the first highlighted time window. Each arm visibly connects shoulder, elbow, neutral wrist and hand. Keep the pen clear of text.
Draw all interface elements in exactly the same frontal plane as glass and bezel, level text baselines, horizontal rules and vertical axes. Schematic diagram exact content: heading "Time samples (schematic)"; beneath it a horizontal short waveform with exactly three equal-width overlapping outlined windows shifted right. First window amber, other two sage. Each window connects down to its own label: "Window 1", "Window 2", "Window 3". Each of those connects down to ONE corresponding column of a three-column spectrogram. Spectrogram x axis labeled "Time", y axis labeled "Frequency", dark-to-light scale labeled "Magnitude". Highlight only the first column in amber to correspond to Window1, other two columns sage. Footer "One FFT per complete window". No invented numeric findings, no extra windows/columns, no random background plots. Diagram is illustrative, not a claim about actual capture values. Comfortable spacing and readable generous type at 768px. Maintain familiar Lab room, dim inactive peripheral monitors, soft face light, no plants or neon wash. No extra people or floating overlay graphics.
